chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abd al-'Aziz al-'Abdi, from 'Ubayd ibn Zur'arah, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding the saying of the Mighty and Majestic: 'So whoever of you sees the month, let him fast it.' He said: 'How clear it is: 'Whoever sees [i.e., is present in] it, let him fast it, and whoever travels, let him not fast it.'

key_terms.شَهِدَ: To witness or be present; in this context, it denotes residency or being present in one's home region, as opposed to traveling.
key_terms.عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ: Mighty and Majestic (a title for God)

ai.seo_question: What does the word 'shahida' mean in the context of fasting in Ramadan according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) offers a linguistic exegesis of the phrase 'man shahida minkum' in Surah Al-Baqarah, interpreting 'shahida' (witnessed) as implying physical presence or residency. This clarifies the jurisprudential basis for the exemption of travelers (*musafirun*) from fasting, establishing that the obligation is tied to being present in one's home region. This interpretation underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on deriving legal rulings from the precise semantic nuances of the Quranic text.
